An acceptable salt concentration in a swimming pool is between 2700-3400 ppm (parts per million), with 3200 ppm being the ideal level.
Let's say your pool volume is 100 gallons, and the salt ppm of the pool reads 2000 ppm.
Consider that your desired concentration of salt is 3200 ppm.
When you key in these values, the pool salt calculator will give a result to add 1 lb of salt.
This means that you need to mix 1 lb of salt in your swimming pool to increase the concentration to 3200 ppm.
On the other hand, if the current salt ppm of the pool reads 4000 ppm, that means the concentration is higher than the desired level of 3200 ppm.
In this case, the pool salt calculator would show that you need to replace 20 gallons of pool water with fresh water to bring down the concentration level.
An acceptable range for the salt ppm in a pool is between 2700-3400 ppm, with 3200 ppm being the ideal level.
In order to achieve the recommended salt concentration of 3200 ppm in a 10,800-gallon pool, we need to add about 290 lbs (130 kg) of salt (assuming no salt has been added yet).
